items.text: Entry. Anyone who joins a brand's newsletter list (site signup, checkout opt-in, or an import marked as new) gets the Day 0 welcome about 10 minutes after joining, then the day 2 and day 5 steps. The one exception: a signup that is also a first order gets the Thank-you instead of the welcome (item 3).

changelog.line: Published for approval
Launch with days 0, 2 and 5; day 10 removed for now.
Names the steps' days (2 and 5); day 10 retired (USAGE-DAY10-SPEC).
The welcome arrives about 10 minutes after joining, not on joining (the WELCOME-SKIP-SPEC hold; review R3).
Names the welcome skip: a signup that is also a first order gets the Thank-you, not the welcome (item 3); was "(item 3)" alone, which read as every checkout opt-in getting the welcome.

items.text: Exit on purchase (your W01–W05 request). Any paid order of the brand, before or after joining, stops every remaining Welcome step: someone who has ever bought from the brand is not a non-buyer, so a prior customer who joins gets the Day 0 welcome and none of the steps. The check runs daily, so a step already sent isn't recalled.

changelog.line: Published for approval
The scope stated: any paid order before or after joining, so a prior customer who joins gets the welcome and none of the steps (the Klaviyo shape; documentation reconciliation); was "at any time".

items.text: Welcome and Thank-you on the same day. A newsletter list's welcome automation waits at least 10 minutes after each join and skips anyone whose signup is their first order (a same-brand first-order list row from 1 hour before to 10 minutes after the join): they get only the Thank-you. Before 2026-11-07 both sent back-to-back to about 20% of Thirsty Girl and 10% of Ruze sign-ups.

changelog.line: Published for approval
Implemented (WELCOME-SKIP-SPEC): the welcome holds 10 min and skips a first-order joiner; was "currently gets BOTH … Recommended: skip the Welcome".

items.text:
Frequency Risk: Monthly launch overlap (your W04 question). Smart Sending (item 13) withholds a brand's broadcast from anyone who received one of its journey emails in the last 24 hours or has a journey step due in the next 24 hours (a step up to 2 hours overdue still counts), so someone part-way through the Welcome series doesn't get a step and a launch on the same day; on other days they receive both, by design.
Keep the step emails distinct and evergreen (don't restate the month's launches in W04), so there is nothing to duplicate. That is the only practical way to maintain multi-brand, multi-language campaigns at this scale — for the people writing them even more than for the platform.

changelog.line: Published for approval

The same-day stack is addressed by Smart Sending (item 13, SMART-SENDING-SPEC); the editorial instruction stays as the standing practice, no longer a recommendation; was "Nothing suppresses a broadcast … Recommended: Keep the step emails distinct …".
The 24 hours run both ways, as intended: a step due in the next 24 hours also withholds the broadcast; was "in the last 24 hours".
The look-ahead also covers a step up to 2 hours overdue, as built.

items.text: No restarts (your completion-tracking question). Every follow-up step sends once per person, ever — even if they unsubscribe and later re-subscribe. The one exception: the Day 0 welcome DOES send again on re-subscribe. That's deliberate. A re-subscribe is a new sign-up after a real opt-out; coming back from a hold (item 21) is not one and sends no welcome.

changelog.line: Published for approval
The "confirm you want it" question dropped: accepted 2026-11-05.
A re-subscribe (a new sign-up after a real opt-out) distinguished from a return from a hold (item 21): only the first sends the welcome again.

items.text: Unsubscribing from any email of a brand unsubscribes them from every marketing list of that brand, so it stops every remaining step of both series.

changelog.line: Published for approval

Broadened to the brand: an unsubscribe from a step, trigger or ask email now reaches every marketing list of the brand, not just the newsletter list, so it stops the remaining steps whichever email carried the link.

items.text: Ruze's 15-day step. Done: Ruze's former 15-day campaign is now its Day 2 “Product Value / Why Choose Us” step, and nobody who already received it is sent it again.

changelog.line: Published for approval
The Day 2 step named by Kaylinn's title (Product Value / Why Choose Us); was "Gentle conversion reminder".

How it was done: the recommendation said retire the 15-day campaign and re-schedule it; what was done is a transition of the same list and journey, reconfigured from 15 days to 2 and renamed, which achieves "without re-sending" by construction (everyone who received it is still on the list, and a step sends once per person).

Implemented: list 56 "Ruze No purchase 2 days" (the former 15-day list) and its running campaign are the Day 2 step; was "Keeps sending as-is. Recommended: … retire the 15-day campaign and re-schedule it as the 2-day step".

items.text: Entry (your transition request). A customer enters on their first paid order EVER with the brand, only if they are subscribed to the newsletter at the time (ticking the checkout opt-in counts). Returning customers get no thank-you and no series. A buyer who isn't subscribed gets only the receipt — no marketing email.

changelog.line: Published for approval

items.text: The clock is delivery, not the order date. Each step is timed from the Aftership delivery confirmation of the first order and sent by the next daily run: “Getting started” the day the package is reported delivered, the day-14 and day-30 steps 9 and 25 days after it. A split shipment runs on the first parcel delivered. A tracked package still in transit waits up to 10 days after the order; an order with an untracked carrier, or never confirmed delivered, falls back to the order date plus 5, 14 and 30 days, so nobody gets stuck. Day 14 is “Get More From Your Purchase”, an educational email and not a review request: the sites have no review functionality yet.

changelog.line: Published for approval
Day 14 becomes an educational "Get More From Your Purchase" email, not a review request (no review functionality on the sites).
Implemented (DELIVERY-CLOCK-SPEC): steps timed from delivery, in-transit wait, order-date fallback; was "The clock is the order date … Recommended: start the clock at delivery".

A split shipment runs on the first parcel delivered; the order-date fallback is for an untracked carrier or an order never confirmed delivered; was "(untracked carriers, split shipments) falls back to the order date".

items.text: Final step skipped for anyone who has ordered again since their first order. A repeat buyer never gets an earlier step late either.

changelog.line: Published for approval

items.text: Returning customers get no thank-you.

changelog.line: Published for approval

items.text:
Frequency Risk: Multiple brands. Overlap is small: about 5% of active newsletter subscribers are on two or more brands' lists and under 1% on three or more (the live figure is on the Dashboard's SES account pane). The industry pattern is a per-person cap by message class, with journeys and transactional email exempt.
A per-person cap is added only if overlap reaches 15%. For broadcasts it will skip, never defer: someone who already got one brand's broadcast that day is skipped from the second brand's, not pushed to the next day, with the tiebreak going to the brand they engage with more. (Klaviyo Smart Sending skips the same way: 16-hour default, per account, no cross-brand awareness.)

changelog.line: Published for approval
The policy stated as standing (no longer a recommendation); the one-off 4.7% replaced by the live measure; was "Overlap today is small: 4.7% … Recommended: Add a per-person cap only if …".
changelog.callout: Monitoring is in place (2026-11-07): the hourly brand health run measures the overlap; the Dashboard's SES account pane shows it with the 12% review and 15% cap-trigger lines, and #integrations-alerts is paged when it crosses 15% from a known reading (the Dashboard shows the live figure in any case).

changelog.line: "Reaches 15%", as the monitor triggers; was "grows past 15%".
changelog.callout: Monitoring is in place (2026-11-07): the hourly brand health run measures the overlap; the Dashboard's SES account pane shows it with the 12% review and 15% cap-trigger lines, and #integrations-alerts is paged when it reaches 15% from a known reading (the Dashboard shows the live figure in any case).

items.text:
Frequency Risk: Per brand. This is where the real frequency risk is (broadcast cadence + two series). A new non-buyer can get the welcome, two No-purchase steps and every broadcast the brand sends in their first 5 days — up to five emails in five days — and a new buyer gets the same shape from the New Customer series. Journeys alone are fine; it's journey steps stacking on broadcasts that creates the concern.
Smart Sending. Per brand, broadcasts only: a broadcast skips anyone who received a journey email from the same brand in the last 24 hours or has a journey step due in the next 24 hours (a step up to 2 hours overdue still counts), decided when the send starts. The campaign page shows how many it would skip before Start, and the skipped count stays on the campaign's analytics and the Campaign Matrix. Journeys are exempt: one-shot and time-bound. Marketing can switch Smart Sending off per campaign for a major launch or a time-sensitive promotion; the Matrix shows "off" on such a campaign (or its skipped count, when it was switched off part-way through a send). (Klaviyo Smart Sending skips the same way, with the same per-campaign switch.)
The same-day double (item 3) is fixed: the one stack that hit every checkout opt-in. Sunset stays the backstop; complaint rates in Brand Health show fatigue first.

changelog.line: Published for approval
Day 10 removed: two No-purchase steps, so the first-days stack is five emails in five days.
Counts follow days 2 and 5 (was three steps, seven emails in ten days); point 2 reads as done (WELCOME-SKIP-SPEC).
Agrees with the 24-hour rule; asks for a per-campaign override for major launches and time-sensitive promotions so those sends are not suppressed by a journey email.

Analysis: Klaviyo's Smart Sending is a per-campaign checkbox, on by default, turned off for flash sales; Braze and Iterable cap globally with a per-campaign "ignore" flag; none shows the skipped count before the send. Chosen: the per-campaign switch, default on, with the would-skip count shown before Start and the skipped count kept on the analytics and the Matrix, so an override is a visible choice. Held for data: skipping the journey step instead (the daily sweep yielding to a broadcast scheduled in the next 24 h, so the cap holds on launch day); read the skip breakdown by journey after ~30 days and decide.
Implemented (SMART-SENDING-SPEC): the 24-hour rule at claim, the per-campaign switch, the before-Start count, Skipped on the analytics and the Matrix; was "Recommended: 1. A Smart Sending rule …".
changelog.callout: Further recommendations are in the History below (2026-11-07): a per-campaign override is built; a journey-side rule that would hold the cap on launch day waits on the first weeks of skip data.

changelog.line: Decided 2026-11-09: when Marketing switches Smart Sending off for a campaign, everyone receives it and that day's journey steps still send; the same-day double is accepted and is Marketing's call. The journey-side rule (the daily sweep yielding to a scheduled broadcast) is retired and will not be built. The look-ahead half is built by SMART-SENDING-LOOKAHEAD-SPEC.
The look-ahead also covers a step up to 2 hours overdue, as built, and "off" never replaces a recorded skip count.

items.text: Language. A campaign's language reaches that language only; English also reaches subscribers with no language on record.

changelog.line: Published for approval

items.text: Who it applies to. Every brand that sends from listmonk, each brand on its own: someone who stops engaging with one brand keeps getting the others. Sunset is switched on when a brand is onboarded; the Sunset column above shows, for each brand, whether it is on. The check runs once daily, at 15:00 UTC (8:00 am Mountain in winter, 9:00 am in summer).

changelog.line: Published for approval
Stated as the onboarding expectation the Sunset column verifies (no brand is exempt); the run time anchored on 15:00 UTC with both Mountain readings.
Sunset is on from onboarding and the Sunset column shows it per brand; was "no brand is exempt; the Sunset column above verifies it" (a policy, not an enforcement).

items.text: What counts as engagement. A click on any of the brand's emails other than its Manage Preferences link (that click says nothing either way; only ticking a held brand on that page counts, item 21), a paid order of the brand (whether or not an email drove it), or an open we can confirm was a person — today, an open through Gmail. Automatic opens (such as Apple Mail's privacy feature) and opens we can't confirm don't count; those subscribers are judged on clicks and purchases. (Klaviyo does the same: clicks and placed orders count, and Apple privacy opens are excluded.)

changelog.line: Published for approval
A click on the Manage Preferences link is not engagement; ticking a held brand on that page is.

items.text: 0–180 days: normal sending. This is the generous end of common practice (90 to 180 days, with 90 the usual starting point), so a subscriber gets twice the usual time before any hold. The strict engagement definition (item 16) and data from the Oct 2026 Younique win-back campaign serve as justification for this expanded window. If complaint rates rise, however, we'll be obligated to shorten it out of necessity.

changelog.line: Published for approval

items.text: Hold at 180 days without engagement. When someone's last engagement (or their sign-up, if they never engaged) is 180 or more days ago (the default window, item 17) and the brand has sent them at least 6 broadcasts since they signed up or last returned from a hold (counted from then, not from their last engagement; a broadcast Smart Sending skipped them from is not counted), they stop getting its regular sends, on every list of the brand (its re-engagement lists aside). Every new engagement restarts the window. This is a hold, not an unsubscribe: no opt-out is recorded, and they move to the brand's re-engagement list. Someone whose first counted broadcast went out before the brand's sunset start date is never held by this rule, unless they return from a hold or unsubscribe and later sign up again.

changelog.line: Published for approval
180 named as the default window (item 17); was "restarts the 180 days".
The six broadcasts are counted from sign-up or the last return from a hold, as the rule counts them; was "at least 6 broadcasts since".
States what the rule does: a hold covers every list of the brand; a broadcast Smart Sending skipped is not counted; and the sunset start-date condition.

items.text: Four emails on a fixed schedule from the hold (at the hold, then 90, 180 and 185 days after it): three re-engagement asks and a confirmation. The days below are those of the default 180-day window; a shorter window moves the whole schedule earlier by the same amount. Each is an automation Marketing builds per brand, sending at once, in each language the brand's subscribers use: day 180 "Reconnect With the Brand", the day someone is held; day 270 a second reminder; day 360 a last chance, with 5 days to respond; day 365 a confirmation that the brand's marketing emails have stopped (an inactivity suppression, item 22), with a Manage Preferences button. The schedule runs whether or not a step's automation exists: a step with no running automation is simply not sent. The Re-engagement circles above show each brand's four automations; the Sunset column shows whether sunset is set up.

changelog.line: Published for approval
Day 365 is the inactivity-suppression confirmation, not an unsubscribe (item 22, Kaylinn's 2026-11-05 note); was "a confirmation that they have been unsubscribed".
The schedule stated from the hold (+90, +180, +185 days); the day numbers are the default window's.
Day 180 named as the guide and Kaylinn's brief name it, "Reconnect With the Brand"; was "We miss you".

items.text: Marketing may send a win-back broadcast to the 180d or 270d list at any time. This changes no one's schedule. The 360d and 365d lists take automations only: the system refuses any broadcast to them, win-back or promotional, so nothing but the last chance and the confirmation can reach anyone past day 360.

changelog.line: Published for approval

items.text: Coming back. Before day 365, any engagement from item 16 (a click, a Gmail-confirmed open or a purchase) returns a held subscriber to regular sends the next day, with no new welcome email; ticking the brand on the Manage Preferences page returns them at once, also with no welcome (a return from a hold, not a re-subscribe, item 5). They remain candidates for any journey they have not yet had: a first paid order after coming back enters the Post-purchase series as usual. Unsubscribing from an ask is a real opt-out, recorded on the brand itself from whichever of its emails carried the link, and they are never asked again on that consent; a later genuine re-subscribe starts a new clock.

changelog.line: Published for approval
Names the Manage Preferences tick as a way back.
Scoped to before day 365 (after it, item 22); the Manage Preferences tick named a return from a hold, not a re-subscribe (item 5), so no welcome.

The ask opt-out is now recorded on the brand's own row whichever email carried the link, so it holds even for an ask whose queue the person has already left; and "never asked again" says on that consent — with the brand confirmed again, a further year of silence starts the clock afresh.

items.text: 365 days: inactivity suppression. 185 days after the hold (365 days without engagement at the default window), the brand's marketing emails to the person stop — recorded as an inactivity suppression, never as an unsubscribe, so the two are always distinguishable — and the confirmation is sent when the brand's day-365 automation is running, whether or not the earlier emails existed: off its re-engagement lists and out of its marketing, but never deleted or blocked. The date rule runs regardless of the asks; Marketing's commitment is that every brand's four re-engagement automations are running before its first cohort reaches day 360 (the earliest is March 2027). Only their own action brings them back: the Manage Preferences button, signing up again, or opting in at checkout — after day 365 a click, an open or a purchase alone no longer does (item 21 covers the days before).

changelog.line: Published for approval
Record day 365 as an inactivity suppression, not a customer unsubscribe, so the two can be distinguished; do not suppress before the re-engagement emails have been activated.

Renamed as she asked: inactivity suppression (the industry's suppression-versus-unsubscribe distinction; the data model already kept the two apart). The date rule stays; her second ask is met as a commitment (four automations running before the first day-360 cohort, March 2027), tracked as a Gate Watch gate. Was "365 days: unsubscribed from marketing …".
Timed from the hold (185 days); 365 is the default window's day; was "After 365 days without engagement (180, then the re-engagement schedule)".
The post-365 way back contrasted with item 21: a click, an open or a purchase alone no longer releases; only the person's own action does.

items.text: Safety check. If a brand's latest broadcast shows zero tracked opens, that day's run skips the brand: broken tracking looks exactly like nobody reading. Holds for bounce problems are handled separately and never get the re-engagement emails.

changelog.line: Published for approval

rows: Regular sends stop; re-engagement emails at 180, 270 and 360 days
Inactivity suppression: marketing emails stop, with a confirmation email
sunset-policy.note: *and at least 6 broadcasts received since they signed up or last returned from a hold. Engagement means a click (other than the Manage Preferences link), a purchase, or a Gmail-confirmed open. Days are the default 180-day window's; the later steps follow the hold at +90, +180 and +185 days.
